strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes selected-candidate fetch and provenance verification continuations replay-safe for headless schedulers by binding replay to the original bounded request identity.
Prevents stale M46 selected-candidate fetch or provenance evidence from being replayed for a different candidate/provenance target that reuses the same continuation id.
Fail-closes before returning checkpoint evidence when the current replay request differs from the authorized request that created the checkpoint.
Persists only bounded request fingerprints in continuation checkpoints and preserves no-duplicate replay without storing raw provenance or candidate material.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.continue_once selected-candidate fetch and provenance verification continuations now replay only when the same continuation_id is paired with the same bounded request fingerprint; mismatched retry input is rejected before old evidence is returned.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M46.1 and M46.2 already execute fetch and provenance verification, but their replay branches previously read checkpoints by continuation_id and returned the checkpoint before comparing the current target request.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless caller could execute request A under continuation_id X, then submit request B with the same id and receive request A bounded evidence for a different candidate or provenance verification target.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M45.1 admitted registry trust, M46.1 fetched the selected candidate, and M46.2 verified provenance; R6.1 changes replay identity validity for those existing continuation checkpoints.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once route is fixed; no new JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase stores bounded request fingerprints in checkpoints and does not add report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, or verdict surfaces.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust runtime recomputes bounded request fingerprints before replaying M46 selected-candidate fetch or provenance verification checkpoints and returns invalid params when the fingerprint is missing or mismatched.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can safely retry selected-candidate continuations across restarts while detecting conflicting retry inputs deterministically instead of silently accepting stale replay evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: Hardens the M46 selected-candidate continuation chain before approval and active replacement continuations depend on replayed fetch/provenance evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: R6.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and archives the R6.1 value gate. Review must confirm this is runtime replay identity enforcement, not a report or readiness wrapper.

exit_criteria: M46.1 selected-candidate fetch checkpoints persist a bounded request fingerprint derived from route kind, continuation id, progress expectation, selection evidence, candidate/provenance/signer fingerprints, and active activation fingerprint.
M46.1 replay recomputes the current fetch request fingerprint and rejects missing or mismatched checkpoint fingerprints before returning old candidate fetch evidence.

M46.2 provenance verification checkpoints persist a bounded request fingerprint derived from route kind, continuation id, fetch checkpoint identity, expected fetch decision, candidate/provenance/signer/active fingerprints, and hashes of request-only provenance statement/signature/public-key material.
M46.2 replay recomputes the current provenance request fingerprint and rejects missing or mismatched checkpoint fingerprints before returning old provenance evidence.
Same-request replay still returns bounded replay evidence without duplicating ModePackCandidateFetched or ModePackCandidateProvenanceVerified ledger events.

Checkpoint and RPC outputs do not expose raw provenance statement JSON, signature, public key, candidate JSON, registry manifest, prompt, provider response, file content, stdout/stderr, command, environment, paths, credentials, or secrets.
No new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, generic network executor, automatic approval, or automatic activation is added.
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_continue_once_fetches_registry_selected_candidate_and_replays proves same-request selected-candidate fetch replay and rejects same-continuation-id fetch replay when target identity changes.
The same Rust behavior test proves same-request selected-candidate provenance replay and rejects same-continuation-id provenance replay when request-only provenance material changes.
cargo check --workspace passes with request_fingerprint checkpoint fields owned by brownie-store and replay validation owned by brownie-runtime.
